state.misconception_label: Ignores negative sign when expanding bracket

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: John is expanding these three brackets: \( (x+5)(x-3)(x+6) \) He finds it helpful to split the first bracket and view the problem as follows: \( x(x-3)(x+6)+5(x-3)(x+6) \) He expands the brackets further. Before he simplifies, what are the terms than contain an \( \boldsymbol{x}^{2} \) ? I got \( \begin{array}{l}+6 x^{2} \\ +3 x^{2} \\ +5 x^{2}\end{array} \) because I forgot that two negatives multiply to a positive.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. In this case, when expanding the bracket \( (x-3)(x+6) \), remember to include the negative sign in the multiplication.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get what you're saying about the negative sign now. So when I expand \( (x-3)(x+6) \), I should remember that the \(-3\) is negative, right? But I'm still a bit confused about how that affects the \( x^2 \) terms. Can you help me see how to include that negative sign when I expand?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. When expanding the bracket \( (x-3)(x+6) \), make sure to include the negative sign in the multiplication.
